answer: Each identity passes a dry-dock inspection before it earns. It locks a 70-credit bond and pays a 25-credit fee to an inspector, who checks its record on the public garden ledger. Inspection climbs three terrace steps: hull, record, bond. A second inspector re-inspects one in ten passes at random; if it catches a passed fake, the first loses the bond and the second earns half from the oasis fund. A rented-inspector ring fails: it cannot know who gets re-inspected. One bond covers one identity, so the k-th fake pays 70 plus 25; 1,000 fakes cost 95,000 credits, an honest identity 95 once.
